## Summary

Codex (GPT-6) built these lossless loading changes and the follow-up to [the Operator's newest review](https://github.com/ryanjosephkamp/splashery/pull/588#issuecomment-6198837043).

Restored main's eager startup globally: removed the opening-pack gate, duplicate pre-renderer scene decode, early scan preparation, and custom help bootstrap. Native app, Player, UI, and help follow the integrated main. PDF-only dependencies no longer block ordinary openings; GIF encoding remains deferred until export.

Sunglasses, Soda can, and Fountain pen now use their original full scan files at every detail setting. Water bottle, Baseball cap, and four museum scans retain exact-data prefixes. Compressed manuals reproduce the current PDFs byte for byte and were refreshed after the final main merge.

## Verification

Merged main d4df5998 additively at 3c904ae8, then refreshed the manuals at d29d9219. Final source d29d9219a60db83c361d32eb897986f7992a1912: **204 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**, across smoke, taps, kit, unit, Real Objects, every load-time spec, and help. 0 spec processes returned nonzero. The captured-toy embed transfer check remains under 30 MB. The earlier measured fallback source separately passed all 190 required tests. The unscoped project suite was not rerun.

[The opening table](https://github.com/ryanjosephkamp/splashery/blob/codex/load-time/docs/audits/load-time-2026-10.md) contains five adjacent alternating pairs per group. Twenty-five groups retain their actual b222e93a pin; three fresh phone groups use 30ed36e5, all against frozen main c13a9d3f. Phone Sunglasses: **2,142.5 → 1,995.4 ms (-6.9%)**; Fountain pen: 2,387.5 → 1,870.3 ms (-21.7%); Soda can: 2,061.2 → 2,157.2 ms (+4.7%). Older prefix samples are superseded and excluded.

The original unchanged Strawberry test ran ten times per source: main 8 passed/2 failed; branch 9 passed/1 failed. Native failure traces show a main return-frame screenshot taking 26.8 seconds inside a 15-second wall-time poll. A separate ten-per-source batch using main's upstream camera/pulse readiness fix passed the Strawberry section 10/10 on both. Two main runs failed later at Lantern; those failures remain recorded. These observations do not establish equal underlying failure rates. Protected smoke assertions, thresholds, controls, and clocks were not edited by this PR.

New startup and full-file regression tests were observed failing before their fixes and passing after. Prior visual evidence retains its actual source pins: 49 of 50 pairs are pixel-identical; desktop Book differs at eight pixels by at most one RGB level. Final Prettier, American English, whitespace, protected-path, and audit-budget checks pass. The complete task audit is **2,952,356 bytes**, strictly below 3,000,000; raw runs remain outside Git. [Receipts and source pins](https://github.com/ryanjosephkamp/splashery/blob/codex/load-time/docs/audits/load-time-2026-10/verification.json).

## Deviations

Measurements use Chromium 151, Linux llvmpipe, three Mesa threads, and a four-core quota with phone/desktop profiles. Physical-phone performance and public per-toy wire transfer remain unmeasured. The original top-20 set and four reviewed toys were measured; the full catalog was not rescreened.

Timing collection predates the last main merge's upstream UI, QR, photo, and manual updates. Those changes were regression-tested but not timed again. No observation is relabeled as measured on the final merged source.

## Known issues

The strict no-slower screen remains unmet: **10/28 groups have higher medians** after the eager fallback. Top-20 local HTTP bodies save **4.1% combined**, and only 1/20 reaches 25% individually. Neither task target is claimed met. A separate fixed same-main control produced 8/12 higher medians (-24.7% to +62.6%) with identical source in both phases; it is separate calibration and does not prove any candidate increase is noise.

## What was cut

Disabled the three phone scan-prefix selections and removed custom engine/help gzip bootstraps. Their unused generated prefix files retain byte proofs but are not requested at runtime. No lossy point-count, texture, precision, camera, engine-version, or animation-clock changes. Protected PLY-column removal remains deferred. Older timing tables and validation receipts are explicitly superseded.

Rule check: E1 — ten unpublished email-metadata commits were rewritten in a prior turn. All subsequent review changes are additive; no force push, main push, PR merge, or ready-for-review action.
title: Codex task 51: lossless opening data and load-time audit
